classification.difficultyReason: Combine marked parallel families, transversals and straight-angle sums across composite diagrams.

content.prompt: Find the value of the pronumerals. You do not need to give reasoning.

spec.description: Two gently rising lines with double internal parallel arrows and two descending lines with single upper-left terminal arrows. All lines extend beyond the intersections. Unfilled sectors show 70° at upper left, a° inside upper right and b° below lower right.
spec.mathematics: Both opposite line pairs are parallel. The upper-left interior angle is 70°. The upper-right interior and lower-right exterior angles are supplementary to 70°.
spec.answerVisibility: Only 70°, a° and b° appear in the question diagram.

answer.worked:
Co-interior angles on parallel lines sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}a+70&=180\\a&=110\end{align*}$$
Corresponding angles on parallel lines are equal, so $b=110^\circ$.

spec.description: Two gently rising parallel lines with right terminal arrows. Two extended transversals meet on the upper line. The consecutive lower sectors there are a°, b°, 80°; the lower-left triangle sector is 50°.
spec.mathematics: The lower line is inclined 10° for drawing. Its left interior angle is 50°; the right side makes an 80° alternate angle with the upper line. The resulting apex angle is 50°. No side-length labels are added.

answer.worked:
Alternate angles on parallel lines are equal, so $a=50^\circ$.
Angles on a straight line sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}a+b+80&=180\\50+b+80&=180\\b+130&=180\\b&=50\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Two steep rising lines with single parallel marks and two shallower descending lines with double marks. At lower left the interior right sector is 85°. At upper left a° is exterior right and b° interior bottom. At upper right d° is interior left and c° exterior bottom.
spec.mathematics: A parallelogram formed by extended lines has adjacent interior angles 85° and 95°. Both parallel families and all five arcs are retained.
spec.answerVisibility: Only 85°, a°, b°, c° and d° appear.

answer.worked:
Co-interior angles on parallel lines sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}b+85&=180\\b&=95\end{align*}$$
Angles on a straight line sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}a+95&=180\\a&=85\end{align*}$$
Using the other pair of parallel lines:
$$\begin{align*}d+95&=180\\d&=85\end{align*}$$
Angles on a straight line give:
$$\begin{align*}c+85&=180\\c&=95\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Two rising parallel lines have right terminal arrows. Separate transversals cross at left and right. Left lower-facing corresponding sectors are a° and 55°; right alternate sectors are 74° and b°.
spec.mathematics: Parallel direction 20°, left transversal 75° and right transversal �����54° produce the stated 55° and 74° sectors. The transversals have no parallel marks and do not meet within the displayed extent.

answer.worked:
$a=55^\circ$ (corresponding angles on parallel lines).

$b=74^\circ$ (alternate angles on parallel lines).

spec.description: Two horizontal parallel lines with right terminal arrows. Extended sloping sides meet on the upper line. Consecutive lower sectors at the apex are b°, c°, a°. Base angles are 47° and 64°.
spec.mathematics: For a freely chosen base of 2.4 drawing units, the apex is determined by base angles 47° and 64°. The apex angle is 69°. All five sectors have unfilled arcs.
spec.answerVisibility: Only a°, b°, c°, 47° and 64° appear.

answer.worked:
Alternate angles on parallel lines give $b=47^\circ$ and $a=64^\circ$.
Angles on a straight line sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}b+c+a&=180\\47+c+64&=180\\c+111&=180\\c&=69\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Two descending parallel lines with upper-left terminal arrows. Two rising transversals meet on the right parallel. The left intersections show 45° and 113°. At the common right vertex b° is upper left, a° is the broad bottom sector, and an offset c° leader identifies the small lower-left sector between transversals.
spec.mathematics: The triangle formed by the transversals and left parallel has interior angles 45°, 113° and 22°. The right descending line is parallel to the left. The c leader is attached to the 22° lower-left sector, distinct from the adjacent a sector.
spec.answerVisibility: Only 45°, 113°, a°, b° and c° appear; no calculated values appear.

answer.worked:
$b=45^\circ$ (corresponding angles on parallel lines).

The corresponding $113^\circ$ angle at the right intersection is vertically opposite $a$, so $a=113^\circ$.

Angles on a straight line sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}b+c+a&=180\\45+c+113&=180\\c+158&=180\\c&=22\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Two horizontal lines have matching internal right arrows. An unmarked left transversal descends right and an unmarked right transversal rises steeply right. d and 64° are corresponding lower-right sectors; 83° and q are corresponding upper-right sectors. No arcs.
spec.mathematics: Left transversal direction −64° and right transversal direction 83° preserve the labelled sectors. The two transversals are not parallel.
spec.answerVisibility: Unknowns d and q have no degree symbols; numerical givens retain degree symbols.

spec.description: Two shallow descending parallel lines with internal rightward arrows. The left transversal has a lower right-angle square and corresponding t above. On the right transversal, 114° and v occupy upper-left corresponding sectors. No ordinary arcs.
spec.mathematics: Parallel direction −16°. The left transversal is perpendicular; the right transversal has direction 50°, giving the upper-left angle 114°. No parallel relationship between transversals is added.
spec.answerVisibility: t and v remain bare italic letters; 114° and the square are givens.

answer.worked:
$v=114^\circ$ (corresponding angles on parallel lines).

The square marks $90^\circ$, so $t=90^\circ$ (corresponding angles on parallel lines).

spec.description: Two rising diagonal parallels with internal arrows. Two different descending transversals cross them. b and 74° occupy corresponding upper sectors on the steeper transversal; y and a square occupy corresponding right sectors on the other.
spec.mathematics: Parallel direction 44°. One transversal is perpendicular; the other has upper arm direction 118°, making 74° with the parallel. Transversals have no mutual parallel marks.
spec.answerVisibility: Only b, y, 74° and the right-angle square appear.

answer.worked:
$b=74^\circ$ (corresponding angles on parallel lines).

The square marks $90^\circ$, so $y=90^\circ$ (corresponding angles on parallel lines).

spec.description: Oblique quadrilateral with top-to-right and left-to-bottom sides marked parallel. Left marked side extends upper left; right marked side extends lower right; bottom-to-right side extends upper right. Top angle 37°, bottom angle 115°, exterior left s and exterior bottom-right t. No arcs.
spec.mathematics: Marked sides have direction −45°. The left joining side gives the top angle 37°; the bottom-to-right side gives bottom interior angle 115°. Drawing lengths are unconstrained construction choices, not givens.

answer.worked:
$s=37^\circ$ (alternate angles on parallel lines).

Let the interior angle at the right intersection be $r$. Co-interior angles on parallel lines give:
$$\begin{align*}r+115&=180\\r&=65\end{align*}$$
Angles on a straight line give:
$$\begin{align*}t+65&=180\\t&=115\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Triangle with a horizontal base and an extended horizontal through its apex. Both horizontals have internal right arrows. Below the upper line are exterior 66° on the left and d on the right. Base interior labels are m and 52°. No arcs.
spec.mathematics: Base angles are constrained to 66° and 52�� by the parallel relationship. The printed 66° is exterior at the apex, not the apex interior angle.

spec.description: Horizontal top and bottom with internal right parallel arrows, vertical left side extending below the base, and a right side sloping down-right. The top extends beyond both sides; the base extends left only. Lower-left interior square, upper-left exterior n, upper-right exterior 70°, lower-right interior p.
spec.mathematics: The left side is perpendicular to the parallel pair. The right side makes a 70° lower-right exterior angle with the top horizontal.
spec.answerVisibility: Only n, p, 70° and the square appear.

answer.worked:
$p=70^\circ$ (alternate angles on parallel lines).

The upper-right angle at the top of the vertical is $90^\circ$ by corresponding angles. Its vertically opposite angle is $n$, so $n=90^\circ$.
